To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
DAGK is catalytically active and stable in micelles composed solely of C(14)-detergents.

lysophospholipids are capable of supporting high catalytic activity and stability of DAGK in detergent micelles, and that the enzyme interacts significantly differently with LMPC micelles than it does with dodecyl-POC micelles.
DAGK can be stabilized in the presence of micelles composed of the lysophospholipids, LMPG, LMPC and LPC.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structure, function, and interactions of membrane proteins.
the interactions of membrane proteins (enzymes) with detergents.
the structural and functional properties of integral membrane enzymes, and in particular with the interactions of these enzymes with detergents.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
DAGK is a lipid-free membrane protein that can be studied in micelles, but that its properties are dependent on both the nature of the detergent and the presence of lipid in the micelles.

the lipid requirement for DAGK is not as stringent as previously thought and that the enzyme can maintain its native-like structure and function in the presence of C(14) lipid-free detergent micellar environments.
the catalytic activity and stability of DAGK in micelle-forming detergents are dependent upon the presence of a C(14) alkyl chain.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
DAGK is a lipid-free enzyme.
DAGK can be stabilized and activated in the absence of lipid, and that the best detergent for this purpose is LMPC.
the enzyme diacylglyceryl kinase (DAGk) is active in detergent micelles composed of a lysophospholipd, lysomyristoylphtadidylcholine, but not in micelles of the corresponding diacylphospholipid.
The main takeaway from our work is that
some membrane proteins may be amenable to structural studies in lipid-free detergent systems, but that the nature of these detergent systems must be carefully considered.
some integral membrane enzymes can maintain their native-like properties and functions in detergent micelles, even in the absence of lipid.
some integral membrane enzymes can maintain native-like catalytic properties and structural integrity in lipid-free micelles.
